en.name: Stephen VII
en.summary: An obscure pope installed during Rome's turbulent "rule of the harlots," when the powerful Theophylacti family controlled papal elections.
en.body: Stephen VII's three-year pontificate fell squarely within the period modern historians call the saeculum obscurum, when the noblewoman Marozia and her family effectively controlled the selection of popes in Rome. Little concrete detail survives of his acts as pope beyond his installation under this system of aristocratic patronage, typical of the poorly documented and politically compromised papacies of the early tenth century.
